description.purpose: The state surfaces of one agent's context assembly: `turns` is the rolling conversation (both user and assistant turns, session-scoped, id lexicographically time-ordered, with a `deferred` lifecycle stamp for mid-round turns - the turns-table sibling of round.fired, never content), `round` is the per-turn fan-in slate that carries the assembled legs (leg-window, leg-memory) and the tool round (assistant tool_call turns, tool results) with the fired flag both guards read. Both carry `session_id`, because the same two tables are also the record of a session until it closes: then they are read back whole, and the delivery is booked in `batched` - the ledger the prune lane trusts.
description.use_when: One per collector hive. No other cell writes here; code cells own no state, so the assembly state machine keeps all of its state in this store.
description.not_in_scope: No durable memory of its own. The rolling window is short-term working state and is cut at READ time (order by id desc, limit N); the durable record of a closed session leaves with the write batch, and what of it is worth remembering is decided by whoever receives that batch, never here. Deletes happen only on the collector's evidence-gated prune chain (GH #76): sessions the `batched` ledger names as delivered and aged, cut up to their close boundary - never a cap, never a schedule of this store's own. No FTS, no vectors, no canonical bindings: nothing here is retrieved by similarity, it is retrieved by recency.
description.emits_meaning: messages[]: one tool_result per op. hop.operation drives the assembly state machine, hop.rows_affected carries the RMW guard signal (a guarded update that affected 0 rows means another emission won the race and this one is terminal).
description.consumes_meaning: messages[]: tool_call turns with store-native args. The lane a reply belongs to is carried by context.store_origin ('collector'), the step by context.col_phase, both promoted by the edge that sent the op.
examples: {operation: insert, table: turns, row: {id, session_id, turn_id, role: 'user', content, recorded_at}} -> the turn is in the window before the window is read
{operation: select, table: turns, columns: [...], where: {session_id}, order_by: [{col: 'id', dir: 'desc'}], limit: 12} -> the turn cap runs in the store, the byte cap runs in the assembler
{operation: update, table: round, set: {fired: 1}, where: {turn_id, role: 'leg-window', fired: 0}} -> rows_affected 1 means this emission owns the fire
{operation: select, table: round, columns: [...], where: {session_id}} -> the whole day's rounds in one read, which is what a session close hands on
{operation: delete, table: turns, where: {session_id, recorded_at: {lte: <close boundary>}}} -> the prune chain cuts a delivered-and-aged session exactly at its evidence; rows_affected is the report
